overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Everything sent through your providers in the last 30 days. Each message went only to people whose consent held when it was sent.

overview.unknown_one: {{count}} message may or may not have been sent
overview.unknown_other: {{count}} messages may or may not have been sent

overview.heldDetail: no yes for that channel at sending
overview.perDayLabel: Messages sent per day by channel
overview.noProviders: No provider is set in messages.yaml yet, so nothing is sent.
overview.linksDetail: Clicks arrive in Analytics with the campaign, so visits and goals count them.
overview.noClicks: No clicks in the last 30 days.

campaigns.description: Every campaign with its audience, channel and results.

campaigns.noAudience: No segment or list yet: make a segment in Audience, or import a list.
campaigns.noAudienceLinked: Audience could not be read; link it in messages.yaml, or import a list.

campaigns.estimating: Asking Consent who may get it…

campaigns.toGo_other: {{count}} still to go; consent is asked for each as it goes.

campaigns.optOutsSince_other: {{count}} people opted out since it was scheduled and are already left out.

journeys.title: Journeys
journeys.description: Messages started by an event, with waits, conditions and channel changes. A person leaves when they convert or opt out.
journeys.noneDetail: A journey starts when your app posts an event, such as signup, or when someone joins a segment in Audience.
journeys.newDetail: Saved as a draft; nobody enters before it starts. Each person enters once.
journeys.name: Name
journeys.goalHint: The event that counts as converted, such as invoice_sent; empty for none.
journeys.goalHintSegment: An event, or segment-left to count leaving the segment as converted.

test.openedNot: Opened none of the emails before?

journeys.testConsentPick: Has consent for a channel now?
journeys.stepsDetail: People now at each step, and who passed it in 30 days.
journeys.triggerEventDetail: Posted by your app to POST /api/v1/events as {{event}}
journeys.triggerSegmentDetail: A segment in Audience, read every minute
journeys.leavesOptOut: At the end, or on opting out
journeys.pausedDetail: Paused: nobody new enters, and people inside wait at their step until it resumes.
journeys.analytics: Clicks arrive in Analytics under the campaign {{campaign}}.

templates.title: Templates
templates.description: Messages with personal fields such as {{example}}. WhatsApp templates are approved by Meta before they can be sent.
templates.noneDetail: Make one for each message: an email with its subject, an SMS, or a WhatsApp template Meta approved.
templates.dialogDetail: Personal fields are written {{example}}, or {{fallback}} with a word for people without it.
templates.name: Name
templates.subject: Subject
templates.emailHint: Paragraphs at blank lines; [words](https://...) and addresses become links. The unsubscribe link and your postal address are added at the foot.
templates.smsHint: How to stop, from messages.yaml, is added to every SMS that does not say it already.
templates.waNameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and _, as in WhatsApp Manager.
templates.waBodyHint: Read from Meta on Sync; {{one}}, {{two}} are filled from the fields below.
templates.footEmail: Every email carries an unsubscribe link, recorded in Consent at once.
templates.footWhatsApp: WhatsApp: the person can reply STOP at any time.

bounces.title: Bounces
bounces.description: An address that bounces hard is not sent to again until someone fixes it. Three soft bounces in a row count as a hard one.

optouts.title: Opted out here
optouts.description: Every unsubscribe and STOP, kept by Messages and checked before every message, with or without Consent.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: The OpenAsy products Messages works with, and the addresses to give each provider.
integrations.consentDetail: Asked for every person on every channel right before each message, in batches; unsubscribes and STOPs are recorded there.
integrations.consentOwn: consent.check is own: Messages uses only its own opt-out list.
integrations.audienceDetail: Segments to send to and journeys started by joining one; sent, opened, clicked and unsubscribed go back as events. Link Messages in audience.yaml too, so erasures reach it.
integrations.analyticsDetail: Every link carries utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign, which Analytics keeps, so visits and goals count the campaign.
integrations.eventsDetail: Post events that start journeys and count as their goals, with an editor token.
integrations.sesDetail: Subscribe this address (HTTPS) to the SNS topic your configuration set publishes to; it is confirmed on its own.
integrations.smsDetail: Give these addresses for delivery reports and replies. They carry a secret: keep them out of tickets and chats.
integrations.whatsappDetail: The callback address in your Meta app's webhook settings, with the verify token from {{token}}; subscribe to messages and message_template_status_update.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Set in {{file}} with the rest of the install. Shown here as applied; changed in the file, not here.
settings.readOnlyDetail: Edit the file and commit it. The product reads it again within a minute and lists any line it could not apply. Keys stay in environment variables, never in the file.
settings.noFile: # No settings file is applied: no provider is set, so nothing is sent.
settings.notApplied: The file on disk is not applied
settings.providersDetail: Keys are environment variables, never in the file.
settings.consentValue: Asked of Consent before every message, for the purpose {{purpose}}
settings.softBouncesValue_one: {{count}} in a row count as a hard bounce
settings.softBouncesValue_other: {{count}} in a row count as a hard bounce
settings.linksValue: Tagged utm_source={{source}}, the channel and the campaign; clicks counted

auth.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Messages.
auth.accountDetail: Your name, password, second factor and passkeys.
auth.membersDetail: Who may use this Messages, and their role: viewers read, editors make and send, admins manage.
auth.signinDetail: How people sign in: with a password, or through your identity provider.
auth.tokensDetail: Tokens for scripts and the linked products, each with one role and an expiry.
